problem: What is the value of $f(x)=4\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+1$ at its local maximum points?
worked_solution:
On a negative branch of the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x\le -1.
$$

The points where $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=-1$ are local maximums of the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$ 

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\le -1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $4$ and adding $1$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{sec}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\le -1 \\  & 4\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\le -4 \\  & 4\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+1\le -4+1 \\  & f(x)\le -3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=-3$ at the local maximum points.
